I was ready for the hype of this game.  I'm a big supporter of indie games and I had Hades 2 on my wish list.  It's a rogue-like heavy into relationship building.  I get it, this type of genre, its SUPPOSED to be repetitive.  Understandable.  And I wouldn't say it gets "boring" as it gets "tedious" after doing the same run over and over with slightly different weapons or objectives.  The pros are there's lots of creative ways of building relationships with the different NPCs and their is extensive epilogue to unlock that deepens to the story, the con being you will be so inundated with dialogue by that point that you'll be skipping most of it.
Overall it's definitely not for everyone.  It's more of niche genre of gameplay, and to recommend an otherwise well made game would be disingenuous.

By the 100-hour mark, I have successfully reached the epilogue and completed most of the NPC questlines. I am now going for 100% achievements. This is one of the first games I have ever purchased on Steam. Supergiant did a great job with the music and voice acting, especially their portrayal of Hades and the love he has for his wife.

I love the core roguelike mechanics, where each run feels unique and different boon combinations lead to completely different outcomes. Even after 100 hours, there are still many things I haven't tried, such as the other weapons. I finished the main story and epilogue using only the sword, so I am excited to explore the rest of the arsenal. The Heat system keeps the game addictive long after unlocking the main achievements, making it a game with endless replay value.

My personal favorite characters are Artemis, Nyx, and Dionysus. They are always a highlight whenever I encounter them during a run.

The world design across the different regions (Tartarus, Asphodel, Elysium, Greece, and the Temple of Styx) is distinct and visually striking. Seeing Greece for the first time after defeating the final boss was picturesque.

The main boss fight in Elysium was a bit frustrating on initial runs, but it eventually became fun. On the other hand, the main boss of Asphodel felt a bit too easy, even on my first playthrough.

While the game offers a God Mode if the learning curve feels too steep, I recommend experiencing it on the default difficulty.

As for characters I did not connect with as much, Ares stands out. I usually avoid his boons and pick other options instead.

I completed my first five successful runs using a keyboard and mouse, but I switched to a controller after getting one. The story progression feels smooth, making it easy to play for 2 to 3 hours in a single session. It is one of the few games where I do not even keep background yt videos or podcasts playing while I play.

I have not bought the sequel yet, as I want to get 100% achievements on this one first, but I cannot wait to play Hades 2. I would easily recommend this game to any fan of Greek mythology.
